definition: Flexible spending account (FSA) is an employer-sponsored benefit account funded primarily through voluntary salary reduction agreements. Employees elect to contribute a portion of their pre-tax earnings, which the employer withholds and deposits into the FSA. Employers may also choose to contribute, depending on the benefit plan’s terms. Employees may be permitted to adjust or revoke their contribution elections during the plan year, though such changes are generally limited to specific qualifying events unless otherwise allowed by law or by the plan itself. Annual contribution limits are set by the Internal Revenue Service and are periodically adjusted for inflation. FSAs are generally “use-it-or-lose-it” accounts, requiring employees to spend the balance within the plan year. However, employers may adopt one of two options allowed under IRS rules: permitting a short grace period for spending unused funds, or allowing a limited carryover amount into the following plan year. Funds in an FSA may be used to pay qualified medical expenses not covered by insurance, including copayments, deductibles, prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, and medical equipment. Eligible expenses may be incurred by the employee, their spouse, dependents claimed on their tax return, or a child under age 27 at the end of the tax year. FSAs cannot be used to pay health insurance premiums, long-term care insurance or expenses, or amounts already covered under another plan. FSAs provide important tax advantages: employee contributions are not subject to federal income or employment taxes, employer contributions are excluded from gross income, and reimbursements for qualified medical expenses are tax-free. However, FSAs are only available through employer-provided benefit plans; self-employed individuals are not eligible. fixed rate mortgage / flexible spending account (FSA) Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026
